claims.statement: The Bot Platform endpoint verifies X-Bot-Api-Secret-Token via hmac.compare_digest; outside development a missing configured secret returns 503 rather than accepting blind, and dev/test keeps the accept-unsigned behavior for ergonomics.

The OA endpoint accepts only the empty-body URL-verification probe (returns {"status": "verified"} with 200) and does not enforce X-Zevent-Signature on real events because the held oa_secret_key is the OA access-token secret, not Zalo's webhook signing key; POST /zalo/oa/verify-signature remains as a diagnostic for a future cutover.

Both endpoints ack in <1s; webhook-ack latency is sampled into the SLO sliding window via record_webhook_ack_ms((time.time()-t0)*1000), but only successful 2xx acks are sampled; enqueue failure returns 503 so Zalo retries, success returns 200 with the result body.

Only request size and safe event metadata (bytes=N) are logged; candidate content, provider signatures, timestamps, and identifiers never enter application logs and the body is never logged because it can carry candidate text.

ZaloBotChannelAdapter implements TextChannelAdapter + TypingCapability and wraps ZaloBotSender (token rides in the URL path); ZaloOAChannelAdapter implements TextChannelAdapter + ReceiptCapability, wraps ZaloOASender with lazy refresh, strips the oa: storage prefix when calling the OA Send API, and forwards quote_message_id so OA CS replies quote the inbound message.

ChannelAdapterRegistry.register validates the provider id against is_known_provider (typo-proof); get returns the adapter or None (fail-closed), and get_typing/get_receipt return None for absent capabilities which means "do nothing", not "failure".

ChannelDispatchService is registry-driven and provider-neutral; it compares channel_account_generation on the command to the active generation immediately before provider I/O and suppresses stale work across disconnect/reconnect/replacement, while the runtime authority fence on the outbox row remains separate and both must be current for a send to proceed.

After signature verification and before any business write the webhook resolves the runtime authority stamp via InstallationService.resolve_active; the bot token passed to run_zalo_ingress is the DB-resolved token so a token rotation takes effect on the very next request.
